steps.content: Twilight approaches, the last scent of blood carried away on the wind.
The old woman's steps across the sandy earth are both firm and light. After days of long travel, she finally lifts her dust goggles, revealing a pair of stern, penetrating eyes.
From the fortified hill ahead, figures rise one after another from behind sandbags and mounted guns, waving to her with unguarded joy.

steps.speaker: Camp Guard A
steps.content: It's Helga! Helga's back! Lift the lockdown!

steps.speaker: Camp Guard B
steps.content: Should've given us a heads-up, Helga! We'd have rolled out the welcome wagon!

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Heh, save the fuss. Just let 'em know I'm here.
[Scene Change]

Inside the Farland Alliance council tent, the leaders have just concluded a hollow discussion. The real question—whether to bind their future more closely to Fraser—has, since yesterday's incident, been settled in a consensus.

This is the scene Helga walks into. From the seat of honor, Jabara scrambles to his feet, ready to surrender the chair to the rightful authority—the former revolutionary soldier and current Farland Alliance diplomat newly returned from Fraser.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Stay put. You look comfortable there, and I'm good standing. Wouldn't get a clear view of all your faces from way back there anyway.
Her gaze sweeps over the companions she hasn't seen for so long.

There is Yokna, who has governed the rift valley for years, reliable in minor matters, yet maddeningly indecisive when the stakes are high. Jabara, guildmaster of the merchants, has spent a lifetime chasing coin; he lacks vision, but can acquire anything, anytime. And Rael, all impulse and rough edges, but a superb warrior and an even better trainer...

The farlands would not function without them. Knowing their flaws all too well, Helga had instructed them before leaving to convene a proper council on the matter of Fraser and DisCity. Now, as her eyes land on the blackboard at the far end of the tent—the word FRASER stark upon it—a faint conclusion settles in her mind.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Let's hear it. What's the situation?

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: Ahem. We trust you've been well? With the unrest along the route, and no word for so long, perhaps bringing some of our own escort would have been wise in hindsight...

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: Hmph. And who's to say "our own" ain't got DisCity spies mixed in? With her skills, she is safer moving alone. Not all of us need a whole damn guard detail just to cross a road.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: Enough. If our intel on DisCity wasn't shit and Fraser wasn't breathing down our necks, Helga wouldn't have had to risk her neck for us in the first place.
Yokna shoots a glare at the two men—all talk, no substance. She spits out her toothpick and launches into the story of everything that's happened since Helga left.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: Never would've guessed... that kid's Hypatia Campbell. No wonder she knows Aurum Secretum tech like the back of her hand. I liked her—still do—but... the proof's right there.

Helga's brow tightens. She remembers the girl as they met in Fraser days ago, but Margaret never mentioned authorizing a journey this deep into the farland territory. And the man with her... almost certainly a DisCity spy. Then there's also the Luminaris Society to consider...
Her eyes flick toward Saina, hunched in the corner, silently honing her blade without a glance upward.

The Luminaris Society's influence spreads through the farlands on the reputation of its Aurum Secretum Warriors. They already have the people's trust. Add a Disian to the mix, and this situation can only sour.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Seems the schemers got restless while I was away.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: They all think they're hunters. All convinced there's treasure buried out here in these WhiteSands...

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: First they feed off our dead comrades' despair, then they prey on the living's hope. Fine. Can't blame us if we bag the prize before they do.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Step into these swallowing sands, and be ready for 'em to be your grave.
She steps to the blackboard and begins methodically laying out the intelligence gathered since her infiltration of Fraser City.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: DisCity hasn't won. But we haven't lost, either. What matters now is this: neither DisCity nor Fraser has a damn clue where the Hypercube veins are since the Black Ring vanished.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: That Black Ring, the one our farland kin poured everything into, is just gone. It's not that they won't tell us. They don't know where it is, either.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This "Unity Gala" is nothing but a consolation prize. A peace offering to shut us up.
The tent, after days of heated argument, falls abruptly silent. The leaders' eyes meet in flickers, then dart away.
Hands clasped loosely before her, Helga meets each gaze in turn, steady and deliberate, reading the unspoken conflict on every face.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: At least Fraser's still trying to get on our good side. They get it. We're all tied together. Sink or swim as one. They wouldn't just ditch the farlands when things get rough. Why else send that Society rep here to show off their Hypercubes?

Though her voice carries a hint of hesitation, Yokna continues to argue for the value of the Luminaris Society's Hypercube technology. Her people need that mine, and her determination to secure them is absolute.

steps.speaker: Jabara
steps.content: Can we trust any of it? What if... Fraser's just looking for a polite way to back out of their promises?!
Jabara's mind works with the volatile speed of a market ticker, churning out ideas that defy all conventional logic.

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: **** 'em all!

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: How many times have those DisCity mutts ground us into the dirt?! The only reason the farlands are still on a leash is 'cause we got no real way to fight the Mania. If it weren't for the Aurum Secretum tech, we'd all be corpses already.

steps.speaker: Rael
steps.content: That Black Ring that can mine Hypercubes was paid for in Furorian blood. And then it just happens to get lured right to the DisCity border? Whose damn scheme is this, huh?
Rael... Guess there's no point in even trying.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Farland Alliance... From the very first day, I've never once seen you all stand as one.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But this time... you've really outdone yourselves.
Helga swallows her rebuttal. With a silent, inward sigh, she turns to leave, only for Yokna's voice to cut through the tent's tension.
Yokna draws herself up, extracts a briefing document from her coat, and lays out their next plan.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: We've captured that DisCity Outland Affairs Officer who showed up after. Calls herself Margaret Kervoz. She's already secured in our rock prison.

steps.speaker: Yokna
steps.content: Care to question her?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...The DisCity Outland Affairs Officer?
[Scene Transition: Exterior]
Rock Prison

A fortress of stone and despair. Prison cells are gouged into the sheer cliff face, each sealed by a heavy, steel-reinforced door. The only opening is a small ventilation window, its frame so savagely eroded by relentless wind and sand it has nearly melted away.
Beyond that barrier is nothing but a sheer, hundred-meter drop. The sole access is a rickety hanging cage. To leave otherwise would require wings.
Inside one cell, the prisoner appears almost serene. With slender fingers, she delicately peels open a withered grain to feed a small bird resting in her palm.
The groan of the prison door breaks the quiet. She turns her head and smiles.

steps.speaker: Margaret
steps.content: I'd almost thought you'd forgotten me. I'm pleased you've decided to visit at last.
